name: Juniper Bonsai
hook: Juniper bonsai dying indoors? It needs to live outside.

steps.title: Outdoors, full sun all day
steps.tip: Keep it on a sunny balcony, not a windowsill. Bring it inside only for a few hours to enjoy it.

steps.title: Water when the top is dry
steps.tip: Feel the soil first, then water until it drains. In summer sun that may be daily. Never keep it soggy.

steps.title: Give it a cold winter rest
steps.tip: It needs a cool winter rest. Below -2°C, move it to an unheated shelter, like a shed, but don't warm it.

steps.title: Feed weakly while growing
steps.tip: Use a balanced liquid fertilizer at low strength every 2 weeks while it grows, and stop in autumn.

steps.title: Repot every 2–3 years
steps.tip: Every 2–3 years, trim the roots and repot into gritty bonsai soil, during the growing season.

steps.title: Hose off spider mites
steps.tip: Spider mites love junipers. Spray the leaves hard with water each time you water to keep them away.

outro: Full sun outdoors and a cool winter: it's a tree, not a houseplant.

sources.title: NC State Plant Toolbox: Juniperus procumbens
NC State Extension Master Gardener: An Audio Introduction to Bonsai With Harold Johnson
Virginia Cooperative Extension: The Art of Bonsai

faqs.question: Can I keep my juniper bonsai indoors?
faqs.answer: Not for long. It is an outdoor tree that needs sun all day and a cool winter rest. Bring it in only briefly to show it off, then put it back outside.
